senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning of term meaning literally: ‘to hunt, to trap,’ not occurring in the NT) to acquire information about an error or fault, with the purpose of causing harm or trouble
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is possible to retain the figurative meaning of ‘trap’ or ‘catch,’ but in a number of instances other figures are used, for example, ‘to cause to trip,’ ‘to cause to fall,’ ‘to hear wrong words from his mouth,’ or ‘to use his words against him.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: the quality of modesty, with the implication of resulting respect
strict conformity to a norm or standard, involving both detail and completeness

animal looking like a longhaired dog with a pointed nose and a bushy tail; either reddish with white underparts (fox) or yellowish brown with red tips to the fur on the back (jackal); scavenger; associated with destruction and devastation, and also with being insignificant but self-important; also intelligent and quick-witted, crafty
senses.comment: Though the Greek term ἀλώπηξ and the corresponding Hebrew terms used in the OT may refer to either a fox or a jackal, ἀλώπηξ in the NT seems to refer primarily to a fox (see Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 31-32, for certain significant distinctions between foxes and jackals).|In areas of the world where the fox is not known, one can sometimes speak of ‘a small wild dog’ or ‘an animal like a small wild dog.’ In other instances translators have borrowed the term ‘fox’ from a dominant language in the area and have then explained the appearance and habits of the animal in a glossary.|For ἀλώπηξ in a figurative sense as applied by Jesus to Herod Antipas, see 88.120.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀλώπηξ[a] ‘fox,’ 4.10) a wicked person, probably with the implication of being cunning and treacherous
senses.comment: Some scholars, however, suggest that ἀλώπηξ in Luke 13:32 may imply ‘worthlessness.’|Rendering ἀλώπηξ in Luke 13:32 by a term meaning ‘fox’ may sometimes be misleading, since in some cultures the fox is regarded as a particularly wise animal, and therefore referring to a person as a fox may be a compliment. A local term for ‘fox’ may have other connotations which are quite undesirable. For example, in some languages a term for fox is used to designate a male or female prostitute, usually of the lowest grade.

senses.def: a general state of distress and trouble
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is no term meaning a general state of distress or trouble, but one can usually speak of such trouble by a verb phrase or clause, for example, ‘that which causes trouble,’ ‘what is hard to live with,’ or ‘what makes people suffer much.’

senses.def: an obligation of a compelling nature
necessity as a law of human experience
pertaining to what cannot be counted
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘countless’ is ‘so many that no one can count’ or ‘so many that there are no numbers left.’

senses.def: (the Greek equivalent of the Latin proconsul) an official ruling over a province traditionally under the control of the Roman senate
an instrument with a sharp-edged head and a handle, used in chopping wood

senses.subdomain: Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
senses.def: the removal of someone from a particular association
senses.comment: In rendering this clause in Romans 11:15, it may be necessary to indicate more specifically the participants and the implied relationships, for example, ‘for if their being rejected meant that people in general were reconciled to God.’

senses.def: the event of ceasing to exist
to rise up in open defiance of authority, with the presumed intention to overthrow it or to act in complete opposition to its demands
senses.comment: It is also possible that ἀποστασία differs slightly in meaning from ἐπίστασις[b] by virtue of the differences in prefixal formation, but there is insufficient contextual evidence to support such a view.

senses.def: to eat a meal, without reference to any particular time of the day or to the type of food involved
senses.comment: In some languages it is impossible to speak of ‘having a meal’ without indicating the time of day or the nature of the food consumed.

senses.def: to eat the earlier meal of the day
senses.comment: Some scholars, however, interpret ἀριστάω in John 21:12 as meaning any kind of meal (see ἀριστάω[a], 23.20), and therefore one would translate as ‘Jesus said to them, Come have something to eat’ or ‘… have a meal.’|In a number of languages the earlier meal of the day may be spoken of as ‘the morning meal’ or ‘the first meal.’ In some languages it is actually called ‘the leftovers meal,’ but see the discussion on meals at different times of the day at 23.25.

senses.def: (derivative of ἀσθένεια[a] ‘weakness,’ 74.23) pertaining to a state of limited capacity to do or be something

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being morally weak and hence incapable of doing good
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἀσθενής in Romans 5:6 as a helpless condition rather than moral weakness (see ἀσθενής[d] 22.3).

senses.def: pertaining to being ill and, as a result, weak and incapacitated
pertaining to a state of helplessness in view of circumstances
senses.comment: The meaning of ‘helpless’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘when we could not do anything about it.’ For another interpretation of ἀσθενής in Romans 5:6, see ἀσθενής[b] 88.117.

senses.def: pertaining to being physically weak
senses.comment: Such a literal translation of this expression in 1 Peter 3:7, however, may be misleading, for in general τῷ γυναικείῳ is interpreted as a reference to one’s wife. Therefore, one may translate as ‘treating with respect one’s wife as the physically weaker partner’ or ‘… as of the weaker sex.’

senses.def: a musical wind instrument consisting of a tube with a series of finger holes used to alter the tone
the capital of Babylonia
senses.comment: Βαβυλών also occurs as a symbol of demonic world power (Revelation 14:8; Revelation 16:19).

senses.def: a gift received as a prize or reward as the result of having won in a competition
senses.comment: In some contexts βραβεῖον refers not to a physical prize or reward but to a spiritual benefit, as in Philippians 3:14 (τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ‘the prize which is God’s call through Jesus Christ to the life above’).

senses.def: a celebration or a festivity marking the anniversary of someone’s birth
a place of detention
senses.comment: Practically all languages have terms for a jail or a prison, though in some instances a descriptive phrase is employed, ‘a place where people are tied up’ or ‘a place to be chained.’ In some instances, highly idiomatic expressions are used, ‘a place for eating iron’ or ‘a room with rats.’

senses.def: to remain in an association for a period of time
to continue in an activity or state
to continue to exist
(derivative of διερμηνεύω[a] ‘to translate,’ 33.145) a person who interprets or translates
to cause something to be or to become false as the result of deception or distortion
to set down in writing in order to keep an account of something
to listen to someone, with the implication of heeding and responding to what is heard
glosses: to pay attention to what is said

senses.def: to obey on the basis of having paid attention to
senses.comment: Terms expressing the concept of ‘obedience’ may frequently be rendered in some languages as ‘to do what one says’ or ‘to carry out someone’s orders.’

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: (derivative of ἐκλέγω[b] ‘to choose,’ 30.92) that which has been chosen
the evidence, normally based on argument or discussion, as to the truth or reality of something

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: a position in front of an object, whether animate or inanimate, which is regarded as having a spacial orientation of front and back

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: a position on the front surface of an object
(with the genitive) marking a participant whose viewpoint is relevant to an event

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being guilty for having done wrong (primarily a legal term)
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘being guilty’ is expressed in terms of the justification for an accusation. Accordingly, this expression in 1 Corinthians 11:27 may be rendered as ‘he can rightly be accused of sinning against the Lord’s body and blood.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being guilty and thus deserving some particular penalty
pertaining to being subject to the control of someone or of some institution
senses.comment: In this context one may render ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας as ‘slaves’ and then render the whole expression as ‘as many as were slaves all their lives because of their fear of death’ or ‘… because they were afraid to die.’

senses.def: to destroy and thus eliminate
senses.comment: It is possible in Acts 3:23 that ἐξολεθρεύω refers to a type of severe ostracism.

senses.def: to put a garment on over existing clothing
glosses: to put on an additional garment

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: pertaining to recurring on a daily basis
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐπιούσιος in Matthew 6:11 as meaning ‘necessary for existence’ or ‘that which is needed for each day’ or ‘that which is needed for the following day’ or ‘… for the future.’ One reason for the difficulties involved in determining the meaning of ἐπιούσιος is the fact that, as Origen stated, it may very well have been coined by the Gospel writers.|For another interpretation of ἐπιούσιος in Matthew 6:11, see 67.206.

senses.subdomain: Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
senses.def: pertaining to a day which is the same as the day of a discourse
senses.comment: For several other meanings of ἐπιούσιος, see 67.183.

senses.def: one who has personally seen an event and thus has personal knowledge and can be expected to attest to the occurrence of such an event

senses.subdomain: Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
senses.def: pertaining to that which causes someone to be pleased
(derivative of εὐφημία ‘to praise,’ 33.356) pertaining to deserving approval or good reputation
senses.comment: In a number of languages ‘worthy of praise’ may be rendered as ‘what people should praise.’

senses.def: to cause to live
(derivative of θαυμάζω ‘to be amazed,’ 25.213) pertaining to that which causes or is worthy of amazement and wonder
a relatively large and elaborate seat upon which a ruler sits on official occasions
senses.comment: In some languages ‘throne’ is rendered as ‘the seat of judging’ or ‘the seat of decision-making for a ruler.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of θρόνος[a] ‘throne,’ 6.112) a ruling power, with the implication of royal status
senses.comment: Most scholars understand θρόνος in Colossians 1:16 as meaning a supernatural power, whether angelic or demonic (see 12.44), but it is possible that θρόνοι in Colossians 1:16 means human rulers.

senses.def: (title for supernatural forces and powers) a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
position of power and authority to rule
senses.comment: There are serious complications in attempting to translate θρόνος in Luke 1:32 literally as ‘throne,’ since this might refer specifically to the seat on which David earlier sat. It may in fact be necessary to translate this expression in Luke 1:32 as ‘the Lord God will cause him to rule in the way in which his ancestor David ruled.’

senses.def: the place from which authority or rule is exercised
senses.comment: In Hebrews 4:16 the phrase τῷ θρόνῳ τῆς χάριτος is clearly a reference to God, and therefore in a number of languages it may be necessary to translate ‘let us therefore with boldness approach God, who shows grace.’
‘It did not have moisture’ (Luke 8:6) may be expressed as ‘there was no water in the soil’ or ‘the ground was not wet.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to do that which is evil or wrong
senses.comment: For another interpretation of κακοποιέω in Mark 3:4, see 20.12.

senses.def: to cause harm or injury to someone or something (a highly generic meaning involving a wide range of harm and injury)
senses.comment: In translating terms meaning ‘to harm’ or ‘to injure,’ it may be necessary to specify suffering, for example, ‘to cause people to suffer’ or ‘to cause people to have pain.’|For another interpretation of κακοποιέω in Mark 3:4, see 88.112.

senses.def: to gain control over someone and thus make such an individual subservient to one’s own interests
glosses: to cause someone to be subservient to
to cause to be like a slave

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κατασκάπτω ‘to dig down,’ not occurring in the NT) to tear down or destroy by digging down into or under
the process of burning
senses.comment: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in the use of terms for burning. For example, the burning of a substance for light, as in the case of a lamp or candle, may be indicated by a term quite different from an expression indicating the destruction or burning up of something. Similarly, the burning of wood for cooking may require still another term. The extent or size of the fire involved may also require some distinctions in terms for burning.

senses.def: the state of being in better health after a previous state of relative lack of health

senses.subdomain: Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
senses.def: (derivative of κρύσταλλος[a] ‘crystal,’ 2.46) to shine in the same way that crystal shines

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: to cause oneself to not be known, with the implication of concealment and secrecy
senses.comment: In some languages this expression in Mark 7:24 may be rendered as ‘he was not able to keep people from knowing where he was’ or ‘he was not able to keep secret where he was.’

senses.def: to not recall information and thus to lose sight of its significance
senses.comment: In a number of languages the fact of ‘forgetting’ or ‘not remembering’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to lose out of one’s heart,’ ‘to have one’s thoughts walk away,’ or ‘to have words disappear from one’s liver.’

senses.def: to not have knowledge about or to be unaware of something, with the implication that something can readily escape notice or be hidden
pertaining to attractive and convincing speech
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand λόγιος in Acts 18:24 as meaning ‘learned’ (see 27.20).

senses.def: pertaining to one who has learned a great deal of the intellectual heritage of a culture
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand λόγιος in Acts 18:24 as meaning ‘eloquent’ (see 33.32).

senses.def: an area in a city or town where meat was sold
senses.comment: Μάκελλον would normally be a particular part of the ἀγορά (57.207).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to become intoxicated

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time following another point
(derivative of μνημονεύω[a] ‘to think about again, to remember,’ 29.7) an instrument or means designed to cause to remember
glosses: something to cause people to remember
senses.comment: In translating Acts 10:4 it is important to avoid implying that God had forgotten; the implication is simply that prayers and acts of charity are means by which God becomes aware and thus responds to such events.|It is also possible to restructure the meaningful components of this statement as in the case of TEV, “God is pleased with your prayers and works of charity.”

senses.def: an aromatic oil extracted from a plant called nard
senses.comment: Translators normally borrow the term ‘nard’ but employ some type of classifier, for example, ‘a perfume called nard’ or ‘a sweet-smelling substance, nard.’

senses.def: to command and give leadership to a household
a dream as a means of communication
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are different terms for ‘dream’ depending upon the nature of the dream. A frightening dream without special significance or a dream with erotic implications may be referred to by terms which are quite different from a term referring to a dream which carries important meaning, in other words, a dream which constitutes a type of vision or symbol of some reality.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being holy in the sense of superior moral qualities and possessing certain essentially divine qualities in contrast with what is human
pertaining to being dedicated or consecrated to the service of God
senses.comment: In some languages it is essential to distinguish between ἅγιος and ὅσιος when these refer to God (see 88.24) and when they refer to persons or objects which have been consecrated to the service of God. It is both theoretically and practically advantageous to make a significant distinction in meaning on the basis of these contextual differences which occur in the Greek NT. It is not difficult to translate ἅγιος and ὅσιος by expressions meaning ‘dedicated to God,’ ‘devout,’ ‘pious,’ etc., but it may be extremely difficult to translate ἅγιος and ὅσιος when applied to God. In some languages one can only use an expression such as ‘he who is truly God’ or ‘he who is in every respect God.’

senses.def: the divine matters which have been promised
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand τὰ ὅσια in Acts 13:34 as meaning ‘divine decrees’ or ‘decrees made by God.’

senses.def: (diminutive of παῖς[a] ‘child,’ 9.41, but in the NT παιδάριον has seemingly lost at least most of this diminutive force, but may have retained some implications of affectionate concern or interest) a child, normally below the age of puberty
senses.comment: Note that παιδάριον in John 6:9 denotes merely a child; it is the referential pronoun ὅς which indicates masculine gender, and therefore one may translate ‘boy.’|It is also possible that in this context the diminutive παιδάριον carries some connotation of endearment.

senses.def: to refuse to listen to and hence to disobey
senses.comment: It would be a mistake to translate παρακούω[a], παρακοή, and παραιτέομαι[e] as meaning nothing more than ‘not to listen to.’ The meaning is clearly ‘to refuse to listen to’ or ‘to refuse to pay attention to,’ and hence ‘to disobey.’ It may therefore be best in a number of instances to translate ‘to refuse to obey.’

senses.subdomain: Pass, Cross Over, Go Through, Go Around
senses.def: to pass by some point of reference as one travels
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of 1 Corinthians 16:7 in the form ‘I do not want to see you just briefly as I travel past’ may be misleading, for it might imply that Paul simply did not want to have a glance at the people as he travelled past. In fact, the negative in this expression may result in serious misunderstanding, and therefore it may be better to translate ‘I want to have an opportunity to talk with you as I travel on through’ or ‘I wish to visit you at least for a while as I journey on.’

senses.def: cardinal number, where there are five hundred instances of a countable entity
to carry around from one place to another
a large number of countable objects or events, with the probable implication of some type of grouping

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a casual non-membership group of people, fairly large in size and assembled for whatever purpose
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is no term corresponding to ‘crowd.’ One may, however, usually speak of such a group of people as ‘many people’ or ‘many men and women.’ Depending on the context, it may besary to indicate some relative difference in size, for example, ‘very large crowd’ or ‘many, many people.’ If the crowd is relatively small, one may sometimes speak of ‘just some people.’

senses.def: an additional name for Pilate
to continue to move forward

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to advance in days) to be quite advanced in age
to add something to an existing quantity
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is not at all difficult to speak of ‘adding things,’ but to add events may provide some special difficulties in restructuring. For example, in Luke 3:20 it may be important to translate as ‘he had done many other bad things, but he also did this,’ and in Galatians 2:6 it may be helpful to translate ‘for those who were of repute did not say that I should do anything more than I was doing.’

senses.def: to ask someone for advice
senses.comment: In rendering ‘to ask advice of,’ one may often employ an expression such as ‘to ask what one should do’ or ‘to ask, What shall I do?’

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the front part of the human head
(a figurative extension of meaning of πρόσωπον[a] face, 8.18)
the two-dimensional surface of an object
senses.comment: In a number of cases one does not translate πρόσωπον in the sense of ‘surface’ since it is an implied component of other terms. For example, the phrase ‘on the earth’ implies the surface of the earth.

senses.def: the form or characteristics of something as seen
(a figurative extension of meaning of πρόσωπον[a] ‘face,’ 8.18) the personal presence of an individual at a particular place

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: a position in front of an object, whether animate or inanimate, which is regarded as having a spacial orientation of front and back

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: face to face) the position of one person facing another, with the implication of direct, personal interaction
senses.comment: The implication of this idiom in 1 Corinthians 13:12 is that there will be clear understanding, and in some languages it is necessary to shift somewhat the figurative expression. For example, it may be necessary to render this passage as ‘how we now understand is like seeing a dim image in a mirror, but then we shall understand as clearly as though we were seeing face to face’ or ‘… as though we were seeing something directly.’

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to see into the face) to judge on the basis of external appearances
glosses: to judge on the basis of appearance
to pay no attention to a person’s status
to judge on the basis of reputation
senses.comment: In some languages an equivalent of this expression in Matthew 22:16 may be ‘when you judge, you look into a man’s heart’ or ‘when you judge you see more than a person’s face’ or ‘when you judge a person, who he appears to be doesn’t count.’

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: before the face, equivalent in meaning to πρό[b] ‘before,’ 67.17, but a somewhat more elaborate phrase rhetorically) a point of time, possibly only a short time before another point of time
(a Semitic idiom, literally: to fix one’s face) to make a decision, with emphasis upon finality
glosses: to make up one’s mind definitely
senses.comment: In order to express the meaning of ‘to decide firmly,’ it may be useful in some instances to translate ‘to decide and to refuse to change one’s mind’ or ‘to decide and not to change.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: those things according to the face) that which seems to be so

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to take face) to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
senses.comment: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to admire the face) to praise someone, normally in an exaggerated or false manner and with insincere purpose
(derivative of Ρώμη ‘Rome,’ 93.563) a person who lives in or is a native of Rome or a citizen of the Roman Empire
a Christian of Thessalonica who was a companion of Paul
to leap or jump, as a possible expression of joy and happiness
senses.comment: For a difference of semantic focus see 25.134).|In Luke 1:41 σκιρτάω may be regarded as an instance of figurative usage: ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ αὐτῆς ‘the baby leaped for joy in her womb.’|Though it may seem quite natural to speak of ‘leaping for joy,’ in some cultures this would not be a meaningful combination of words, for leaping might suggest anger, ritual exorcism (driving out demons), or preparation for war. It may, therefore, be necessary in some languages to translate ‘jump for joy’ merely as ‘be exceedingly glad.’ It may be particularly awkward to speak of a fetus jumping in the womb, for obviously it would simply be a rapid movement of the limbs and not actual change of location. Therefore, it may be better to translate in some instances ‘moved quickly to show joy’ or ‘… as a sign of happiness.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of σκιρτάω[a] ‘to jump for joy,’ 15.243) to be extremely happy, possibly implying in some contexts actually leaping or dancing for joy
senses.comment: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνω τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε ‘be glad when that happens and dance for joy’ Luke 6:23, but see also 15.243 for a different semantic focus. The phrase ‘for joy’ clearly expresses ‘reason,’ and therefore it may be useful to translate ‘dance for joy’ as ‘dance because I am so joyful’ or ‘… so happy.’

senses.def: (derivative of σπουδή[b] ‘to endeavor,’ 68.63) pertaining to intense effort in accomplishing some goal

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: pertaining to being earnest and diligent in undertaking an activity
senses.comment: In a number of languages eagerness can only be expressed in terms of desire. Hence, for Philippians 2:28 one must sometimes translate ‘I am all the more desirous of sending him to you.”

senses.def: to become both dark and gloomy, with the implication of threatening
senses.comment: In order to combine the components of στυγνάζω, which involve not only darkness but also gloom and threatening, it may be possible to translate as ‘dark and threatening’ or ‘so dark as to cause one to be afraid.’

senses.def: to experience an emotional state of both grief and discouragement, as evidenced in the appearance of one’s face
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand στυγνάζω in Mark 10:22 as meaning ‘to be shocked, to be appalled’ (see 25.222).

senses.def: to experience an emotional state of great surprise because of something which appears incredible and alarming
senses.comment: For a different interpretation of στυγνάζω in Mark 10:22, see 25.286.

senses.def: to come to be similar in form to something else
glosses: to share in having the likeness of
to take on the same form as
senses.comment: In some languages a more appropriate equivalent of this expression in Philippians 3:10 may be ‘to come to be like him in his death’ or ‘to die in a manner similar to his death.’

senses.def: to come/go into together with
to correspond to something else in certain significant features
senses.comment: In a number of languages συστοιχέω in a context such as Galatians 4:25 may be best rendered as ‘points to’ or ‘is really talking about,’ so that one may render this expression in Galatians 4:25 as ‘Mount Sinai … really points to the present Jerusalem’ or ‘Hagar … really points to the present Jerusalem.’ The full form of Galatians 4:25 may be rendered as ‘Hagar, who stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia, represents the present Jerusalem.’

senses.def: male bovine; large ruminant animal with horns and cloven hoofs; used for sacrifice and for meat, as a beast of burden, or for pulling a cart or a plow
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘bull’ is simply a generic term for cattle to which is added a specific designation such as ‘male.’

senses.def: pertaining to being of considerable value or worth
senses.comment: It is possible to interpret λίθους τιμίους in 1 Corinthians 3:12 as a unit which means ‘precious stones’ (see 2.29), but in this figurative context of a foundation, the reference may very well be more general.

senses.subdomain: Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
senses.def: pertaining to high status, involving both honor and respect
to pick or gather ripe fruit (especially used of grapes)

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to transgress the will and law of God by going beyond prescribed limits
to provide instruction as to what should be done
(an idiom, literally: to put down the neck) willingly and purposely to expose oneself to extreme danger and risk
senses.comment: In some instances one can translate this expression in Romans 16:4 as ‘who showed they were willing to die in order that I could live’ or ‘in order to help me continue to live, they almost died.’

senses.subdomain: Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
senses.def: pertaining to liking or loving what is good
to be so afraid as to shudder or tremble

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.def: a sheet of papyrus used for writing
gold (the most highly valued metal in the ancient world)
senses.comment: Terms for gold are widespread throughout the world even as the presence of gold or knowledge about gold is likewise almost universal. Therefore, there is usually no difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory term for ‘gold.’

senses.def: gold money, gold coin

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
